message.description: What is wrong, in plain words.

ECMA-335 metadata token (table in the high byte, row in the low 24 bits), e.g.
`0x06000001` for the first method. A plain JSON number.

old_name.description: Name before the edit, if any.

oneOf.description: Set the type of an item.

old.description: Type before the edit, if any.

oneOf.description:
Name and/or retype a local variable or parameter of a function. The variable is named by
its storage (`stack:0xffffffffffffffec`, `register:0x38`: the address space and offset a
decompiler token's `varnode` shows, without the size), so the edit survives re-decompiles.

new.description: The override after the edit; absent removes it.

old.description: The override before the edit; absent when there was none.

oneOf.description:
Set, replace or remove a byte patch: replacement bytes laid over the program's bytes at
the anchor's address. Kept in the log so it shows in the history and can be undone; it is
never pushed to the engine (see [`LogOp::is_engine_op`]).

new.description: The patch after the edit; absent removes it.

old.description: The patch before the edit; absent when there was none.

original.description: The program's own bytes there, lower-case hex; as long as the replacement.

oneOf.description:
Define, replace or delete a named type. One op covers `type_define`, `type_edit_field`
and `type_delete`: the whole definition before and after.

new.description: The definition after the edit; absent deletes the type.

old.description: The definition before the edit; absent when the type was new.

LogStatus.description:
Outcome of applying a log entry (decision 27).

oneOf.description: The anchor could no longer be resolved.

end.description: First address after the block (half-open, like [`AddressRange`]).

initialized.description: Whether the block has file or zero contents; uninitialized blocks (like `.bss`) have none.

perms.description: Permissions as three characters, `r`, `w`, `x` or `-` in that order, such as `r-x`.

oneOf.description: Ordinary block, initialized from the file or zero-filled.

Bits are mapped from another part of memory.

Could not run, or stopped for good.

phase.description: Where it is in its life.

ram_bytes.description: Memory used on the computer (RAM) in bytes, summed over the engine's processes.

tok_s.description: Words per second, roughly (tokens per second); `None` before the first reply.

Each card runs its own full copy of the model (Strata replicas).
Split every layer between the cards (llama.cpp row split).

Strata: KRAKEN chooses the main card, the context and the draft layer from the free
video memory each time the model starts. It always runs on one card and names the
second-card choices in its advice.

Strata: a second card keeps extra experts and helps read prompts and answer. In an early
test prompts were read faster, answers about a third slower; a later test with more free
video memory on the main card showed no clear gain for prompts.

Strata: a second card keeps extra experts in a cache that answers use too. Measured slower
than one card on mismatched cards; offered for completeness.

Strata (engines that support it): a second card helps read prompts and stays out of
answering, so answers run at one-card speed.
